subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw own for side-effecting external secret providers under supervised restarts?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally fail startup when required active SecretRefs cannot resolve, but the reported failure shows that fail-fast can amplify credential-provider calls into account-wide rate-limit exhaustion; changing this needs security and product intent.

options.title: Bounded generic startup backoff
options.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff or cooldown policy around required SecretRef activation, keep backend-specific parsing out of core, and update tests/docs for the new failure contract.

options.title: Document operator/plugin responsibility
options.body: Keep startup fail-fast as the core contract and document supervisor restart limits plus external caching resolver patterns such as Varlock for quota-sensitive secret stores.

options.title: Broader external vault design
options.body: Supersede this with a larger SecretRef provider API design for backend-owned batching, circuit breaking, and persistent/delegated cache semantics before changing startup behavior.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic startup backoff
recommendation.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff or cooldown policy around required SecretRef activation, keep backend-specific parsing out of core, and update tests/docs for the new failure contract.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history connection to the SecretRef runtime and gateway activation surfaces that would need policy-aware changes.
